subject: general
question: A man sells potatoes at ₹27 per kg, which he bought at ₹25 per kg. He also uses a faulty weight and each time gives 800 g instead of 1 kg. His actual gain percentage is:
solution:
**Given:**

Selling price = ₹27 per kg

Cost price = ₹25 per kg

Weight discrepancy = 800 g instead of 1 kg

**Formula Used:**

Gain Percentage = [(Selling Price - Cost Price) ÷ Cost Price] × 100

**Calculation:**

Actual selling price for 1 kg = ₹27

But he gives only 800 g for 1 kg.

So, the selling price for 800 g = ₹27

Cost of 1kg = ₹25

But he is giving only 800gm to the customer, So

Cost of 800gm = 25/1000 × 800 = ₹20

⇒ Actual Gain Percentage = [(27 - 20) ÷ 20] × 100 = 35%

**So, his actual gain percentage is 35%.**
